crowded_flag.definition: both fragment radical centres in rings OR parent ring count >= 3
crowded_flag.confound_note: 93 of 95 crowded rows are NOT exact DB rows (crowded x in_db_row = 93/2); the crowded flag is almost a re-label of the out-of-database set.  The in-DB stratum has only 2 crowded rows so the stratified test is uninformative there.

data_supported: Reference channel has by far the widest tail: 260/543 (47.9%) rows exceed 5 kcal/mol, 51 (9.4%) exceed 10, 12 (2.2%) exceed 15; quantum 49/8/3 and learned 71/12/4.
Only 3 rows have all three channels wrong by more than 10 kcal/mol and none by more than 15: the channels fail on largely disjoint rows (union of any-channel>10 is 61 rows).

Both calibrated channels systematically OVERSHOOT in the weak-bond region: for exp<80 quantum 107/147 positive (sign-test p=3.0e-8, bias +1.74) and learned 123/147 (p=3.2e-17, bias +3.12); the overshoot grows as the bond weakens (bias +4.57 and +6.87 for n=18 rows with exp<70, both p<0.01).
The learned channel's extreme tail is almost perfectly one-sided: 24 of its worst-25 errors are overshoots (binomial p=1.6e-6).

The learned channel degrades on polycyclic / crowded parents and this survives the DB-membership confound: within the 212 non-DB rows a parent ring count >=3 raises MAE from 2.71 to 4.23 (n=90 vs 122, MWU p=1.3e-4).

Reference channel extreme tail is bimodal and structurally readable: large POSITIVE errors on strained small rings (obs_0049/0050 C1=CC1, obs_0072 C1C2CC12, obs_0113 C=CC(=C)C, +15 to +21.6) and large NEGATIVE errors on the triarylmethane / tetraphenylmethane family (obs_0508 -33.4, obs_0520 -31.0, obs_0509 -24.7).
suggestive_only: A 'crowded' flag (both radical centres in rings OR ring count >=3) raises MAE for all channels (quantum +0.48 p=0.015, learned +2.13 p=4.3e-11, reference +1.78 p=0.0012) but 93/95 crowded rows are also out-of-database rows, so the unstratified contrast is confounded; it is decisive only for the learned channel.

Heteroatom count, aromatic-ring count and HAC all shift upward in the failure set for every channel (MWU p from 0.02 to 5e-9) but the effects are small (Cliff's delta 0.12-0.43) and the descriptors are mutually correlated.

Reference-channel failure is mildly associated with fewer heteroatoms and MORE rotatable bonds (Cliff's delta -0.12 and -0.11) - opposite in sign to the calibrated channels, but at these effect sizes it is a weak signal.
unresolved: For the quantum channel the crowded/polycyclic penalty disappears after stratifying on DB membership (delta +0.047, p=0.52 within non-DB rows) - at 543 rows the quantum channel cannot be shown to have a steric failure family.
The quantum channel's worst-case direction is NOT established: 9 overshoots vs 8 undershoots among the 17 rows with any channel error >15 (p=1.0), and 17 vs 8 in its own worst-25 (p=0.11).
Reference-channel weak-bond direction is unresolved: 7 positive vs 11 negative for exp<70 (p=0.48) and 16 vs 9 in its worst-25 (p=0.23); its sign test only becomes marginal at exp<80 (p=0.057).
The 'both radical centres in a ring' sub-flag has only n=6 rows: MAE 5.15 vs 2.06 (quantum) but p=0.16 - not resolvable at this sample size.

Whether the triarylmethane/tetraphenylmethane reference undershoots are a transferability failure of the reference channel or errors in the heterogeneous experimental references cannot be decided from this workspace.

The 543 rows are heterogeneous literature values, not repeat measurements, so all tail counts carry an unknown reference uncertainty; a single bad experimental datum would appear as a failure of all three channels at once (only 3 such rows exist).

analysis_units.tail_census: bond observations (543 rows); each row is one experimental bond observation
analysis_units.descriptor_and_flag_tests: bond observations, but descriptors are parent-molecule properties so rows sharing a parent are not independent
